content: Hypomenorrhea, also referred to as hypomenorrhoea, scanty periods, or spotting during periods, is characterized by an abnormally light menstrual blood flow. This condition is the opposite of hypermenorrhea, which is more accurately termed menorrhagia and involves excessive menstrual bleeding. One potential cause of hypomenorrhea is Asherman's syndrome, a condition involving intrauterine adhesions. In cases of Asherman's syndrome, hypomenorrhea or even amenorrhea (the complete absence of menstruation) may be the only noticeable clinical symptom. The severity of menstrual flow reduction in hypomenorrhea is directly related to the extent and severity of the intrauterine adhesions. A study by Toaff and Ballas in 1978, published in Fertility and Sterility, highlighted the association between traumatic hypomenorrhea-amenorrhea and Asherman's syndrome, emphasizing the importance of recognizing this condition in affected individuals.
